So far everything has been made of separate pieces. First atoms: even the
[blast wave](../webgpu-blast-wave/) was a wave of atoms shoving one another. Then
[darts](../webgpu-darts-in-many-dimensions/), [walkers](../webgpu-metropolis-walkers/) and
the [needles of a magnet](../webgpu-ising-model/), all pushed about by chance. This post
has no atoms and no dice.

Drop a pebble in a pond and a ring spreads out. Nothing travels with the ring: the water
only moves up and down a little and the shape of that moving goes on across the pond.
A wave is that shape. It is a thing in its own right and it does things that no single
particle does. It passes straight through other waves and where two meet it can cancel.

The tank below is a sheet of water seen from above. Red is a crest, blue is a trough and
dark is flat. **Click anywhere to drop a pebble** or drag to skim a stone across the water.

Try these:

- _Drop one pebble._ The ring grows and fades. It fades because the same wave has to
  cover a longer and longer circle so each stretch of it gets weaker. **Wavelength** sets
  the size of the splash: a longer one makes a bigger pebble and wider rings.
- _Drop two pebbles a little apart._ Each makes its own ring and where the rings
  cross they add. Crest on crest is a bigger crest and crest on trough is flat water.
  Then they carry on as if the other had never been there.
- _Switch Source to Plane wave._ A straight line of crests marches across the tank from
  the white paddle on the left. It does not fade because it has no circle to spread
  round. **Wavelength** is the distance from one crest to the next.

```{ojs}

}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| column: screen-inset
//| code-fold: true
//| code-summary: "Show code"
{
  // Shared WebGPU boilerplate: setup, buffers and the animation loop (lib/gpu.js)
  const gpu = await import(new URL("../lib/gpu.js", document.baseURI).href);
  const ui = await import(new URL("../lib/ui.js", document.baseURI).href);

  // Controls are read live from their elements, so moving them does not restart
  // this cell.
  const sourceInput = viewof tankSource;
  const wavelengthInput = viewof wavelength;

  const { canvas, device, context, format } = await gpu.setup({
    width: 640,
    height: 360,
    resolution: "auto",
  });
  canvas.style.touchAction = "none";

  // The tank, in cells, and where things sit in it
  const W = 640;
  const H = 360;
  const cells = W * H;
  const groupSide = 16;
  const beachWidth = 24; // cells of damping at each edge
  const sourceX = 28; // the paddle for the plane wave, just inside the beach
  const amplitude = 0.25; // height of the plane wave
  const C = 0.5; // the Courant number: cells a ripple travels in one step
  const wave = 100; // wave speed, in cells a second
  const maxSplashes = 8;

  // --------------------------------------------------------------- the shaders
  const common = `
    struct Params {
      width: u32,
      height: u32,
      courant2: f32,
      sponge: f32,        // damping per step at the very edge of the tank
      edge: f32,          // width of the beach, in cells
      pad2: u32,
      sourceOn: u32,
      sourceX: u32,
      sourceAmp: f32,     // forcing added each step
      sourceOmega: f32,   // radians a step
      sourceStart: u32,   // step at which the source switched on
      rampSteps: f32,
      splashCount: u32,
      gain: f32,
      pad0: u32,
      pad1: u32,
      splashes: array<vec4f, ${maxSplashes}>, // x, y, height, radius
    }

    @group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> params: Params;

    // 0 in open water, rising to 1 at the border: how far into the beach a cell is
    fn beachFraction(x: u32, y: u32) -> f32 {
      let ex = min(f32(x), f32(params.width - 1u - x));
      let ey = min(f32(y), f32(params.height - 1u - y));
      let e = min(ex, ey);
      return select(0.0, (params.edge - e) / params.edge, e < params.edge);
    }
  `;

  const stepModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      ${common}
      @group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read> before: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> now: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(4) var<storage, read_write> after: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(5) var<storage, read_write> clock: array<u32>;

      @compute @workgroup_size(${groupSide}, ${groupSide})
      fn step(@builtin(global_invocation_id) id: vec3u) {
        let w = params.width;
        let h = params.height;
        if (id.x >= w || id.y >= h) { return; }
        let x = id.x;
        let y = id.y;
        let i = y * w + x;
        let here = now[i];

        // Pull towards each of the four neighbours. At the edge of the tank a cell
        // has nothing to pull on that side
        var pull = 0.0;
        if (x > 0u)     { pull += now[i - 1u] - here; }
        if (x + 1u < w) { pull += now[i + 1u] - here; }
        if (y > 0u)     { pull += now[i - w] - here; }
        if (y + 1u < h) { pull += now[i + w] - here; }

        let q = beachFraction(x, y);
        let sigma = params.sponge * q * q;
        var next = (2.0 * here - (1.0 - sigma) * before[i] + params.courant2 * pull) / (1.0 + sigma);

        // The plane-wave paddle adds to the water rather than fixing it
        if (params.sourceOn == 1u && x == params.sourceX) {
          let t = f32(clock[0]) - f32(params.sourceStart);
          let ramp = smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, t / params.rampSteps);
          next += params.sourceAmp * ramp * cos(params.sourceOmega * t);
        }
        // Past the stability limit the numbers grow without bound: stop them
        // overflowing so the picture stays drawable
        after[i] = clamp(next, -1e6, 1e6);
      }

      @compute @workgroup_size(1)
      fn tick() {
        clock[0] = clock[0] + 1u;
      }
    `,
  });
  const stepPipeline = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: stepModule, entryPoint: "step" },
  });
  const tickPipeline = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: stepModule, entryPoint: "tick" },
  });

  const splashModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      ${common}
      @group(0) @binding(2) var<storage, read_write> before: array<f32>;
      @group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read_write> now: array<f32>;

      // A pebble: a dent with a ring round it, added to the surface and not moving to begin
      // with. The ring makes the dent add up to no net water, as a real splash does
      @compute @workgroup_size(${groupSide}, ${groupSide})
      fn splash(@builtin(global_invocation_id) id: vec3u) {
        if (id.x >= params.width || id.y >= params.height) { return; }
        let i = id.y * params.width + id.x;
        var bump = 0.0;
        for (var n = 0u; n < params.splashCount; n++) {
          let s = params.splashes[n];
          let dx = f32(id.x) - s.x;
          let dy = f32(id.y) - s.y;
          let r2 = (dx * dx + dy * dy) / (2.0 * s.w * s.w);
          bump += s.z * (1.0 - r2) * exp(-r2);
        }
        now[i] += bump;
        before[i] += bump;
      }
    `,
  });
  const splashPipeline = device.createComputePipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    compute: { module: splashModule, entryPoint: "splash" },
  });

  const showModule = device.createShaderModule({
    code: `
      ${common}
      @group(0) @binding(3) var<storage, read> now: array<f32>;

      struct Out {
        @builtin(position) position: vec4f,
        @location(0) uv: vec2f,
      }

      @vertex
      fn showVertex(@location(0) corner: vec2f) -> Out {
        return Out(
          vec4f(corner, 0.0, 1.0),
          vec2f(corner.x * 0.5 + 0.5, 0.5 - corner.y * 0.5),
        );
      }

      @fragment
      fn showFragment(in: Out) -> @location(0) vec4f {
        let w = params.width;
        let h = params.height;
        let x = min(u32(in.uv.x * f32(w)), w - 1u);
        let y = min(u32(in.uv.y * f32(h)), h - 1u);
        let i = y * w + x;

        let flat = vec3f(0.10, 0.10, 0.10);
        let v = now[i] * params.gain;
        let crest = vec3f(1.0, 0.282, 0.204);   // #FF4834
        let trough = vec3f(0.22, 0.60, 0.85);
        var colour = mix(flat, select(trough, crest, v > 0.0), clamp(abs(v), 0.0, 1.0));
        colour *= 1.0 - 0.45 * beachFraction(x, y);
        if (params.sourceOn == 1u && (x == params.sourceX || x == params.sourceX + 1u)) {
          colour = vec3f(0.92);
        }
        return vec4f(colour, 1.0);
      }
    `,
  });
  const showPipeline = device.createRenderPipeline({
    layout: "auto",
    vertex: { module: showModule, entryPoint: "showVertex", buffers: [gpu.squareLayout] },
    fragment: { module: showModule, entryPoint: "showFragment", targets: [{ format }] },
    primitive: { topology: "triangle-list" },
  });

  // --------------------------------------------------------------------- buffers
  // Three height arrays that take turns: one step ago, now, and the one being made
  const heights = [0, 1, 2].map(() => gpu.storageBuffer(device, new Float32Array(cells)));
  const clock = gpu.storageBuffer(device, new Uint32Array(1));
  const snapshot = gpu.storageBuffer(device, new Float32Array(cells));
  const paramBuffer = device.createBuffer({
    size: 16 * 4 + maxSplashes * 16,
    usage: GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM | GPUBufferUsage.COPY_DST,
  });
  const paramBytes = new ArrayBuffer(16 * 4 + maxSplashes * 16);
  const paramU32 = new Uint32Array(paramBytes);
  const paramF32 = new Float32Array(paramBytes);

  // Bind groups for each way the three arrays can be taking turns
  const stepGroups = [0, 1, 2].map((r) =>
    device.createBindGroup({
      layout: stepPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
      entries: [
        { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: paramBuffer } },
        { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: heights[r] } },
        { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 1) % 3] } },
        { binding: 4, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 2) % 3] } },
        { binding: 5, resource: { buffer: clock } },
      ],
    }),
  );
  const tickGroup = device.createBindGroup({
    layout: tickPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
    entries: [{ binding: 5, resource: { buffer: clock } }],
  });
  const splashGroups = [0, 1, 2].map((r) =>
    device.createBindGroup({
      layout: splashPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
      entries: [
        { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: paramBuffer } },
        { binding: 2, resource: { buffer: heights[r] } },
        { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 1) % 3] } },
      ],
    }),
  );
  const showGroups = [0, 1, 2].map((r) =>
    device.createBindGroup({
      layout: showPipeline.getBindGroupLayout(0),
      entries: [
        { binding: 0, resource: { buffer: paramBuffer } },
        { binding: 3, resource: { buffer: heights[(r + 1) % 3] } },
      ],
    }),
  );
  const cornerBuffer = gpu.unitSquare(device);

  // ------------------------------------------------------------------- the state
  let turn = 0; // which of the three arrays is "one step ago"
  let stepCount = 0;
  let sourceStart = 0;
  const pebbles = []; // [x, y, height, radius] waiting to be dropped

  // The splash is as wide as the wavelength allows, so the slider sets its size too.
  // A small one is given a little more height so that its rings stay visible
  const drop = (x, y, height = 2) => {
    const radius = 0.375 * wavelengthInput.value;
    pebbles.push([x, y, height * Math.sqrt(6 / radius), radius]);
    if (pebbles.length > maxSplashes) pebbles.shift();
  };

  // Pebbles and drags
  let lastDrag = null;
  const place = (event) => {
    const box = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    return [((event.clientX - box.left) / box.width) * W, ((event.clientY - box.top) / box.height) * H];
  };
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerdown", (event) => {
    canvas.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
    lastDrag = place(event);
    drop(...lastDrag);
  });
  canvas.addEventListener("pointermove", (event) => {
    if (!lastDrag) return;
    const here = place(event);
    if (Math.hypot(here[0] - lastDrag[0], here[1] - lastDrag[1]) > 10) {
      lastDrag = here;
      drop(...here, 1.4);
    }
  });
  const release = () => (lastDrag = null);
  canvas.addEventListener("pointerup", release);
  canvas.addEventListener("pointercancel", release);

  // What the chart is built from
  const readback = gpu.readback(device, [{ buffer: snapshot, bytes: cells * 4 }]);
  const sampleEvery = 10; // frames between readbacks
  const keep = 400; // samples kept for the chart
  let frameCount = 0;
  let epoch = 0; // bumped when the tank is cleared, so a read in flight is dropped
  let peak = 0;
  let startStep = 0; // step at which the latest pebble dropped, or the paddle started
  const heightHistory = []; // {r, peak}: largest wave height against distance travelled

  const [heightHost] = charts.children;
  const draw = ui.plotter(Plot);

  function drawCharts() {
    // A ring spreads over a circle that grows with its radius, so its height should
    // fall as 1/sqrt(r). The dashed line is that, matched to the first point past 40
    const first = heightHistory.find((d) => d.r >= 40);
    const spreading =
      sourceInput.value === "pebbles" && first
        ? [40, 400].map((r) => ({ r, peak: first.peak * Math.sqrt(first.r / r) }))
        : [];
    draw(heightHost, {
      height: 200,
      x: { label: "distance the wave has travelled (cells)", grid: true, type: "log", domain: [10, 400] },
      y: { label: "largest wave height", grid: true, type: "log", domain: [0.01, 3] },
      marks: [
        Plot.line(spreading, {
          x: "r",
          y: "peak",
          stroke: "currentColor",
          strokeOpacity: 0.7,
          strokeDasharray: "4 3",
        }),
        Plot.line(heightHistory, { x: "r", y: "peak", stroke: "#FF4834", clip: true }),
      ],
    });
  }

  function onData(buffer) {
    const u = new Float32Array(buffer);
    let top = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < cells; i++) top = Math.max(top, Math.abs(u[i]));
    peak = top;
    const r = (stepCount - startStep) * C;
    if (r > 10) heightHistory.push({ r, peak: Math.max(top, 1e-4) });
    if (heightHistory.length > keep) heightHistory.shift();
    drawCharts();
  }

  // Empty the tank
  function clear() {
    epoch++;
    const zeros = new Float32Array(cells);
    for (const buffer of heights) device.queue.writeBuffer(buffer, 0, zeros);
    pebbles.length = 0;
    heightHistory.length = 0;
    peak = 0;
  }

  function changeSource() {
    sourceStart = stepCount;
    startStep = stepCount;
    heightHistory.length = 0;
    if (sourceInput.value === "pebbles") drop(W / 2, H / 2);
  }

  const on = (element, handler) => {
    element.addEventListener("input", handler);
    invalidation.then(() => element.removeEventListener("input", handler));
  };
  on(sourceInput, changeSource);
  on(wavelengthInput, () => (sourceStart = stepCount));

  drop(W / 2, H / 2);

  const clearButton = ui.button({ label: "Clear", onClick: clear });
  const readout = ui.readout();
  drawCharts();

  let owed = 0; // steps due but not yet done
  let lastTime = null;
  const groups = { x: Math.ceil(W / groupSide), y: Math.ceil(H / groupSide) };

  function frame(ms) {
    const dt = lastTime === null ? 0 : Math.min((ms - lastTime) / 1000, 0.1);
    lastTime = ms;
    const lambda = wavelengthInput.value;
    const planeOn = sourceInput.value === "plane";

    owed += (wave / C) * dt;
    const count = Math.min(Math.floor(owed), 40);
    owed = Math.min(owed - count, 1);

    const splashes = pebbles.splice(0, maxSplashes);
    if (splashes.length) {
      startStep = stepCount;
      heightHistory.length = 0;
    }

    paramU32[0] = W;
    paramU32[1] = H;
    paramF32[2] = C * C;
    paramF32[3] = 0.3 * C; // damping per step at the edge: a wave crosses the beach once
    paramF32[4] = beachWidth;
    paramU32[6] = planeOn ? 1 : 0;
    paramU32[7] = sourceX;
    paramF32[8] = (4 * Math.PI * C * C * amplitude) / lambda;
    paramF32[9] = (2 * Math.PI * C) / lambda;
    paramU32[10] = sourceStart;
    paramF32[11] = (3 * lambda) / C;
    paramU32[12] = splashes.length;
    paramF32[13] = 2.5;
    splashes.forEach((s, n) => paramF32.set(s, 16 + 4 * n));
    device.queue.writeBuffer(paramBuffer, 0, paramBytes);

    const encoder = device.createCommandEncoder();
    const compute = encoder.beginComputePass();
    if (splashes.length) {
      compute.setPipeline(splashPipeline);
      compute.setBindGroup(0, splashGroups[turn]);
      compute.dispatchWorkgroups(groups.x, groups.y);
    }
    for (let s = 0; s < count; s++) {
      compute.setPipeline(stepPipeline);
      compute.setBindGroup(0, stepGroups[turn]);
      compute.dispatchWorkgroups(groups.x, groups.y);
      compute.setPipeline(tickPipeline);
      compute.setBindGroup(0, tickGroup);
      compute.dispatchWorkgroups(1);
      turn = (turn + 1) % 3;
    }
    compute.end();
    stepCount += count;

    const sample = !readback.pending && ++frameCount % sampleEvery === 0;
    if (sample) {
      encoder.copyBufferToBuffer(heights[(turn + 1) % 3], 0, snapshot, 0, cells * 4);
      readback.copy(encoder);
    }

    const pass = gpu.beginRenderPass(encoder, context);
    pass.setPipeline(showPipeline);
    pass.setBindGroup(0, showGroups[turn]);
    pass.setVertexBuffer(0, cornerBuffer);
    pass.draw(6);
    pass.end();
    device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]);

    if (sample) {
      const mine = epoch;
      readback.read((buffer) => {
        if (mine === epoch) onData(buffer);
      });
    }

    if (frameCount % 6 === 0) {
      readout.textContent = `largest wave ${peak.toFixed(2)}`;
    }
  }

  gpu.run(invalidation, device, frame);

  // The canvas with the controls laid over its corner
  yield ui.stage(canvas, [
    sourceInput,
    wavelengthInput,
    clearButton,
    readout,
  ]);
}
```

## Analysis

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| column: page
charts = {
  // An empty host; the simulation cell above draws into it as data arrives
  const ui = await import(new URL("../lib/ui.js", document.baseURI).href);
  return ui.chartHosts(["height"]);
}
```

The largest wave height in the tank against how far the wave has gone, both on a
logarithmic scale. After a pebble the line falls along the dashed one, which is the
height of a ring that gets weaker as $1/\sqrt{r}$ because the same wave has to cover
a circle whose length grows with $r$. The height squared is what a wave carries and
it is shared out round that circle. On a log scale a power is a straight line, here
with a slope of $-1/2$. Near the end the line drops faster where the ring reaches the
beach. A plane wave has no circle to spread round so its line is flat.

## How the computer makes ripples

The tank is a grid of 640 by 360 cells and each cell holds one number: the height of the
water there. The rule is the same one a ball on a spring follows. A cell is pulled
towards the average of its four neighbours and it carries on moving the way it was
already going. That is all a wave is in the end: each cell is pulled by its neighbours,
and they are pulled by it.

To step forward in time the rule needs three things for every cell: its height now, its
height one step ago and the heights of its four neighbours now. The GPU takes one thread
per cell, all 230,400 of them at once and writes each cell's new height into a third
array. Then the three arrays swap roles with no copying: "the one before" becomes
"the one before that", "now" becomes "the one before" and the new heights become
"now".

At the edges the tank has beaches. Close to the border the rule gets a little damping
that grows towards the edge, so a wave that reaches it slowly dies instead of bouncing
back. Without them the surface soon becomes a mess. Real ripple tanks often have
sloping edges or sponge for the same reason.

## The wave equation

With the height written $u(x, y, t)$ and the wave speed $c$, the wave equation is

$$\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \, \nabla^2 u.$$

On a grid with spacing $\Delta x$ and time step $\Delta t$, each cell is updated with

$$u^{n+1}_{ij} = 2 u^n_{ij} - u^{n-1}_{ij} + C^2 \sum_{\text{4 neighbours}} \left( u^n_{\text{nb}} - u^n_{ij} \right),$$

where $C = c \, \Delta t / \Delta x$ is the Courant number: the distance a ripple travels in
one step in cells. Here it is 0.5 and it cannot be much bigger as
[a later post](../webgpu-courant-number/) explains.

Next [the tank gets a wall](../webgpu-two-holes-in-a-wall/) with holes in it.
